messages.subject: ctmm spatial reference issue
parts:
Hi All, 

I have managed to produce some home range estimates with the ctmm package however I am having issues with it recognising the spatial reference of the input coordinates and instead it is defaulting to the 2D plane of the as.telementry function. 

I have tried defining the CRS using the following code: 
tag <- as.telemetry(t100.2, projection = crs("epsg:32630")) Minimum sampling interval of 1 minutes in t100

However the new x and y coordinates that are produced still have no spatial reference. 
timestamp longitude latitude t x y 1 2019-03-22 00:34:00 56.514 -5.169 1553214840 8723540 -1128111

I can run through all the ctmm code with no issues and produce a home range estimate, however I can't then project it into QGIS becasue of this problem. Also because there is  apparently no spatial data associated to the points, the coordinates also look like they haven't maintained the correct pattern.

I was hoping someone might be able to ched light on how to fix this if there is a fix?

I appreciate this is quite a difficult issue to explain so please let me know if you need any further explanations / information. 

Thanks for your help,
Charlotte

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: ctmm spatial reference issue
parts:
Hi Charlotte,

The projection argument of as.telemetry() is for the output coordinates: help('as.telemetry')

For data frames, the input data are assumed to be in Movebank format, which would either have the input coordinates in long-lat (potentially needing the datum argument) or in UTM with a UTM zone column. Alternatively, if the input data are in an sp-based move object, then they can be in any projection.

After you have your data imported into a telemetry object, you can see the projection information with projection() and you can also export the data into formats for use in QGIS.

Not seeing any other messages or warnings, I'm assuming your data contained long-lat coordinates, which were imported and projected to epsg:32630.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: [ctmm-user] Re: ctmm spatial reference issue
parts:
Hi Charlotte,

Your projection needs to be in meters for the output units to make any sense. epsg:32630 appears to be in degrees.

Also, for epsg:32630, it appears that the default datum of "WGS84" is correct and should not be changed. I throw an error when a straight long-lat projection is used, but I haven't coded this to interpret EPSG projections yet, but I'll add it to the to-do list.

Tell me if that fixes your issues.

Best,
Chris
